title: Can a website hear you through your microphone?
sources: W3C WebRTC Media Capture and Streams Security

lines.text: Have you ever talked about buying hiking boots, and suddenly your phone shows ads for hiking boots everywhere?
It feels like your phone is eavesdropping on your vocal conversations.
lines.caps: Feels like your *phone | is spying on every *word

lines.text: Security researchers have thoroughly analyzed network packets and found apps rarely secretly stream your voice.
lines.caps: Researchers found apps *rarely | stream live *voice recordings

lines.text: Modern mobile operating systems strictly require explicit microphone permissions, displaying an orange privacy dot.
lines.caps: Operating systems show an *orange dot | whenever mic is *active

lines.text: The reality is far creepier: ad tracking networks don't need your microphone.
They predict your desires by combining your GPS location, browsing history, and what your nearby friends just purchased.
lines.caps: They combine *GPS data | shopping habits, and *friend activity

lines.text: The predictive data algorithms are simply so frighteningly accurate that they don't even need to listen.
lines.caps: Data algorithms *predict you | better than a *wiretap!
